case_name: Sabareenath M.S vs Neethu M on 3 March, 2016

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: SABAREENATH M.S., aged 30 years, S/O. SIVARAMAN, husband
parties.respondent_defendant: NEETHU M., aged 25 years, D/O. K.A.MANOHARAN, wife

facts_of_case: The parties are husband and wife who got married. The husband filed a petition for divorce. The trial court granted the divorce. The husband appealed to this court.

legal_principles.principle: The presumptions under Section 27 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 read with Order V Rule 19A of the Code of Civil Procedure are rebuttable.
legal_principles.held: It is always open to the defendants to rebut the presumption by leading convincing and cogent evidence.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure — Order V Rule 19A

legal_principles.principle: The advisability of effecting substituted service is primarily for the trial Court to decide.
legal_principles.held: Order V Rule 20 clearly says that substituted service can be allowed when the Court is satisfied that the conditions warrant such a situation.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure — Order V Rule 20

legal_principles.principle: If an application under Order IX Rule 13 of CPC for setting aside an ex parte decree of divorce is not filed within the period of 30 days, the other party in whose favour the ex parte decree is passed has a right to remarry after the expiry of the said period.
legal_principles.held: This judgment was delivered in the light of Section 15 of the Hindu Marriage Act.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure — Order IX Rule 13
cited_cases: Kuldip Kumar Lal v. Suman Rani, (2012) KHC 2948

legal_principles.principle: By contracting a second marriage, the interest of the second wife intervenes and all the proceedings of the courts can and must take conscious cognizance of events and developments subsequent to the initiation of proceedings.
legal_principles.held: In that case, the petitioner has sought for annulment of marriage and according to the petitioner, at the time of filing the petition, the wife was mentally ill and was admitted in the Government Mental Hospital, Jaipur and was undergoing treatment for schizophrenia.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure — Order IX Rule 13
cited_cases: Surendra Kumar v. Kiran Devi, C.R.P.No.56/1996
P.Venkateswarlu v. Motor And General Traders, (1975) AIR SC 1409

outcome.final_order: The appeal is allowed. The marriage between the parties is dissolved.
